sentences.text: This part adds up most inputs with fixed weights: an international plan raises a typical customer's chance of leaving from about 1% to about 18%, and a voice-mail plan lowers it to below 1%.
More voice-mail messages raise it steadily, from about 1% at 0 to about 6% at 32 messages, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.
A higher evening charge also raises it steadily, from about 1% at 11.76 US dollars to about 2% at 22.57 US dollars, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

Through it, the state moves the chance from about 1% in West Virginia to about 5% in Washington and about 4% in Nevada, and to below 1% in Rhode Island, Hawaii and Vermont (72 to 82 training customers per state).
This part adds up two parts: an early rise and a late rise in calls to customer service.

From about 3 calls upwards it adds to the chance slowly at first, then faster: for a typical such customer, 4 calls take it from about 1% to about 10%, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement

confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
